Ah, it's time to plan the year. Let me think about what I'm doing...

My land is only 3.5 mu total, not much. I keep about 2 mu for wheat-maize — that's the double crop, you plant wheat in October, cut it in June, then straight into maize. The other 1.5 mu I keep in cotton, on the drier piece near the road. Been doing it this way for years now.

**Wheat** — I already planted it last October, so now it's just about managing it through spring. I used the improved seed from the agricultural store, same as most folks around here. Cost me maybe 5 yuan a jin. For fertilizer, before planting I put down one bag of compound (that 15-15-15 stuff, about half a bag per mu). Now in spring when it starts jointing I'll topdress with urea — maybe 15 kg per mu, that's what my brother-in-law does and his wheat always looks good. I'll irrigate twice from the well — once at green-up and once at heading. Water's expensive with the electric pump but you can't skip it or the grain won't fill. Last year I got about 420 kg per mu. Should be similar if the weather's normal.

**Maize** — Right after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste. I'll hire the neighbor's tractor for quick rotary tilling, costs about 40 yuan per mu, but there's really only 3-4 days before planting. I use hybrid seed, the Zhengdan-type one the village shop sells. Put urea at planting and again at the big-trumpet stage, maybe 20 kg each time on the 2 mu. One irrigation if July is dry. If I see armyworm I'll spray once. Hoping for 450 kg per mu.

**Cotton** — This is the hardest. Plant end of April after the soil warms. Cotton eats a lot of fertilizer — I put compound before planting and then urea twice during the season. Need to spray for bollworm two or three times, can't avoid it. The picking is what kills you — that's all family labor, me and my wife, sometimes the kids if they're home from school. Cotton price has been so-so, but I keep planting it because that piece of land doesn't do well in maize.

Money is tight. I can't buy all the fertilizer I'd want. I do what I can afford and hope the weather cooperates.
